findings.where: First screen, the action row: the filled blue 'Write to me' button and the underlined address 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com' beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's one action does nothing. 'Write to me' looks like a filled button and even has a hover rule, and the address is underlined like a link, but neither opens an email when clicked. The only working email link is the small one in the footer, at the very bottom of a long page.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has decided to contact Mark. They click the obvious button or the underlined address, nothing happens, and they may decide the site is broken before they ever reach the footer. Mark loses the enquiry the homepage exists to get.

findings.where: First screen, the 'Book a consultation' button next to 'Write to me' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: There is a second filled button with the same colour, shape and size as 'Write to me', so the first screen offers two equal main actions instead of the one the brief asks for. Booking is also a service the brief and rules never mention. The button links to #consult, and no consultation section appears anywhere on the page, so the click goes nowhere a visitor can see.
findings.who_objects: The visitor, who has to guess whether to write or to book, then clicks 'Book' and finds no booking. The founder and Mark also object: the brief allows one direct, personal way to reach him, and the button promises a booking flow that a brochure site with no bespoke software will not have.

findings.where: First screen, the blue margin notes: 'Istanbul, 2025 / Best Practices in PPP Legislation…', 'Melbourne, 2026 / LLM Course on PPP Law…' and 'São Paulo, 2024 / New Approaches to Risk Allocation…' (desktop left margin; inline between paragraphs on phone)
findings.fault: The talk titles are set in the house blue, which the page's own palette card gives to links and the action. But they are plain text: clicking a title does not open the talk or its slides. On phone they sit as blue lines between the paragraphs, which looks even more like links.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants to see Mark's Istanbul or São Paulo talk taps the blue title expecting the paper, and nothing happens. They are left unsure what on the page is clickable, including the real links.

findings.where: Top navigation: 'Profile', 'Articles and Presentations', 'Blog' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The three nav links point to #profile, #articles and #blog, but the page has no sections with those names. Clicking them either does nothing or drops the visitor somewhere unrelated, so the nav does not reach anything.
findings.who_objects: A visitor checking Mark's background before writing to him clicks 'Profile' or 'Articles and Presentations' and gets nothing. These are the pages that would prove his experience.

findings.where: Specimen section labels in the left margin: 'Palette / Three colours, no accent', 'Type / Newsreader and Public Sans', 'Texture / None', 'Article page / Blog No. 8…', 'Motion / One element enters…', 'Tile notes / For the founder and Mark'
findings.fault: These static section labels use the same blue the page gives to links, so throughout the tile, link blue also means 'section label'. One colour ends up carrying two functions.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging whether this type and colour system will hold up on the live site. When labels share the link colour, a reader can no longer use the colour to tell what is clickable.
